ledger.note: c. 203: the Abhiras capture the Nasik region from the Satavahanas. Infobox: "Period 203 to roughly 270 or 370 CE" (the basis of 203 is not given); Satavahana page: "During Yajna's last years, the Abhiras captured the northern parts of the kingdom, around Nashik region", with Yajna ruling 170-199 (Sen) and his reign ending 181 (Higham): the page's own dates are earlier than 203.

ledger.note: c. 249: Ishwarsena starts the Abhira era and rules Khandesh and Ashmaka. "Ishwarsena started an era to commemorate his ascension in 284 or 249 AD"; his controlled areas "included Lata, Aparanta, Khandesh, and Ashmaka (Andhra), with Nasik as the core"; "about A.D. 250 the Satavahanas were replaced by the Abhiras in Western Maharashtra". The page gives no year for the acquisition of each region; 249 is the era start.

ledger.note: c. 249: Ishwarsena rules Aparanta and Lata. The Ishwarsena page lists both among his areas but gives no date or previous owner; the Kshatrapa counterpart is the Abhira page's ("Abhira chiefs served as generals" of the Western Satraps; Malwa "taken from the Kshatrapas"). Cliopatria keeps the Western Satraps over Lata throughout (102 of its cells) and draws the Konkan as Satavahana to 223 (216 cells at 203) and almost stateless afterwards (32 Satrap cells).

notes: New state Cliopatria lacks (the sa-02-b and sa-02-c reports ask for it). Four pages opened (budget 2-5). The dates conflict: infobox 203 to "roughly 270 or 370"; Ishwarsena, "founder", ascends in 249 (or the page's 284); the Satavahana page puts the Abhira capture of the north in Yajna's last years (before 199); the Abhira page also says the Abhiras rose "after the demise of the Satavahanas" (c. 224). The dossier starts at 203 (infobox) to agree with satavahana-dynasty /ledger (loss c. 203) and ends at 370. Not drawn because the pages do not date them: Malwa (taken from the Kshatrapas, "may"), the Saurashtra branch (the page's date "second half of the 10th century A.D." is a slip), the Vakataka seizure of most Abhira lands, the defeat by the Kadamba Mayurasarman, the tribute to Samudragupta (Allahabad Pillar). Whether the Traikutakas are a branch of the Abhiras is reported as a theory; this dossier keeps them separate. Gazetteer names needed: Lata (region), Ashmaka (region), Anjaneri, Thalner, Trikuta (all used only as text, one coordinate radius or capital).
